title: Gallai–Roy theorem: chromatic number forces a long directed path
statement: (Roy, 1967; Gallai, 1968.) Let $D$ be a digraph on a finite, nonempty vertex set $V$, and suppose the underlying simple graph of $D$ has chromatic number $k$. Then $D$ contains a directed path — a directed walk $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_\ell$ whose consecutive vertices are joined by arcs $v_{i-1} \to v_i$ and whose vertices are pairwise distinct — of length at least $k - 1$, that is, with $\ell \ge k - 1$ arcs.
hypotheses_covered: underlying simple graph has chromatic number k
replaced:
